title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese, meat and dark‑green vegetables, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs cooked without added fat, combined with cheese, lean meat (such as ham or turkey) and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while the vegetables add vitamins, minerals and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most nutrient‑dense foods, containing all essential amino acids.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, which may support natural detoxification processes.
A modest amount of cheese enhances calcium absorption from the eggs.
Cooking without added fat preserves the natural taste of the ingredients and reduces calorie count.
The meal can be prepared in a microwave or a steamer, retaining more nutrients.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: One large egg supplies about 6 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, riboflavin and folate, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Source of vitamin D and selenium
items.content: The yolk is one of the few food sources of vitamin D and also provides selenium, an antioxidant mineral.

items.title: Dark‑green vegetables provide vitamin K and folate
items.content: Spinach and broccoli are high in vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low in added fats
items.content: Absence of added oil reduces overall calories and saturated fat intake.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may develop an allergic reaction to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should moderate egg consumption.

items.title: Sodium in cheese and meat
items.content: Choose low‑salt cheese and lean, minimally processed meat to avoid excess sodium.

items.title: Oxalates in dark‑green vegetables
items.content: Large amounts of spinach can increase the risk of kidney stones in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Beat the eggs, stir in grated cheese, cooked lean meat and pre‑cooked or steamed dark‑green vegetables. Cook on a dry non‑stick pan or in a steamer, stirring until the mixture sets. Garnish with fresh herbs if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep raw ingredients separately: eggs in the fridge at +4 °C, cheese in the dairy compartment, meat in its original packaging for no more than 3 days.
